module_title: Gallantry Awards - Foundational Structure and Core Distinctions
introduction: Gallantry Awards are instituted by the Government of India to honor acts of bravery, conspicuous gallantry, and supreme sacrifice by personnel of the Armed Forces, other lawfully constituted forces, and civilians. In Static GK, understanding their order of precedence and classifications is essential. They are broadly bifurcated into 'Wartime' and 'Peacetime' honors.

core_concepts.title: Wartime Gallantry Awards
core_concepts.description: These are awarded for exceptional acts of bravery displayed in the direct presence of the enemy on the battlefield. The three awards in this category (in descending order of precedence) are: 1. Param Vir Chakra (Highest), 2. Maha Vir Chakra, and 3. Vir Chakra.

core_concepts.title: Peacetime Gallantry Awards
core_concepts.description: These are awarded for acts of courage and self-sacrifice away from the active battlefield (e.g., counter-terrorism operations, anti-insurgency, or internal security rescue operations). The three awards (in descending order) are: 1. Ashoka Chakra (Highest), 2. Kirti Chakra, and 3. Shaurya Chakra.

core_concepts.title: Param Vir Chakra (PVC)
core_concepts.description: India's highest military decoration, translating literally to the 'Wheel of the Ultimate Brave'. It is equivalent to the British Victoria Cross or the American Medal of Honor and is awarded only for the rarest pre-eminent bravery during wartime.

core_concepts.title: Ashoka Chakra
core_concepts.description: India's highest peacetime gallantry award. It is considered the peacetime equivalent of the Param Vir Chakra and carries equal status, prestige, and monetary allowance in the official order of precedence.

important_entities.name: Major Somnath Sharma
important_entities.key_fact: First Recipient of the Param Vir Chakra (1947)
important_entities.significance: Belonging to the Kumaon Regiment, he displayed exceptional valor during the 1947 Indo-Pak war to defend the Srinagar airfield, laying down his life in the line of duty.

important_entities.name: Flying Officer Nirmal Jit Singh Sekhon
important_entities.key_fact: Only Indian Air Force (IAF) Recipient of PVC (1971)
important_entities.significance: Posthumously awarded for his sublime defense of the Srinagar airbase against Pakistani Sabre aircraft during the 1971 war.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common misconception is that gallantry awards are strictly for soldiers. While Wartime awards are almost exclusively military, Peacetime awards—especially the Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra—can be awarded to police personnel, paramilitary forces, and even ordinary 'Civilians' for outstanding bravery.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Param (Param Vir - 1st) -> Maha (Maha Vir - 2nd) -> Vira (Vir Chakra - 3rd).

exam_strategy_tips: Examiners frequently alternate names to test your core understanding. Remember clearly that Param Vir Chakra is exclusively for wartime enemy presence, whereas Ashoka Chakra is for peacetime/counter-insurgency scenarios.
